## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the digest of every tracked file it is given, so a refresh after adding files hides earlier hand edits, which the PR body says verification must detect. Fix this before relying on the refresh command.

## Changes
Adds `refresh_fingerprints`, which rewrites manifest digests for the given names, and `register_new_files`, which adds digests only for names not already in the manifest. Both are in `app/integrity.py`, with new tests in `tests/test_integrity.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Keep existing digests when refreshing after adding files — If you pass a hand-edited `tracked.txt` to `refresh_fingerprints` along with `new.txt`, it replaces the stored digest with the edited file's digest, and `verify` then returns True. Line 17 assigns `entries[name]` without checking whether the name is already tracked, unlike `register_new_files` at line 24. — Any hand edit made before a post-add refresh is silently accepted, which defeats the stated purpose of the manifest. — Fix: Either skip names already in `entries`, as `register_new_files` does, or keep the overwrite behaviour and state in the PR body and docstring that refresh re-baselines tracked files.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_integrity.py:12 — tests — Refresh test cannot catch overwritten edited digests — `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` only refreshes a `tracked.txt` whose content matches its stored digest, so line 17 would pass whether it overwrites existing entries or keeps them. — If the overwrite defect stays or comes back, no test catches it. — Fix: Edit `tracked.txt` before the refresh call, as `test_register_preserves_existing_fingerprints` does, and assert the expected digest and `verify` result.
